sources.entry: The Top 10 Deliverables of Product Managers

summary.title: The Top Deliverables of Product Managers
summary.one_liner: Product managers can be measured by ten concrete deliverables across vision, strategy, design, and execution, from vision narratives and strategy hypotheses to roadmaps, specs, dashboards, OKRs, decisions, and product wins.
keywords: what does a product manager do
takeaways: Write the product vision as a short narrative covering current state, value delivered, future change, and steps to get there, not just a one-line statement.
Treat product strategy as six product/market fit hypotheses (problem, audience, value proposition, competitive advantage, growth, business model) and refine them continuously.
Prioritize the roadmap through four lenses: vision, strategy, customer, and business, since each produces different priorities.
Keep product specs at least covering the problem, target audience, solution rationale, and success metrics, and maintain a few core metric dashboards (acquisition, engagement, monetization).
Document decision rationales so the team trusts the process and can revisit decisions later.
summary.summary: The author, a former Microsoft and LinkedIn product leader, lays out ten deliverables a product manager should own across four dimensions: vision, strategy, design, and execution. Each deliverable gets a short essay-style section explaining why it matters, with examples such as Amazon's 1997 shareholder letter, Slack's vision narrative, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator's refined target audience. The piece is opinionated rather than procedural, offering frameworks (six strategy hypotheses, four roadmap lenses, three core dashboards) instead of step-by-step instructions. It ends by arguing that shipping product wins is the ultimate goal and the other deliverables are tools toward it.
